question: On the fixed spatial reaching task, what do actual PPO/SAC learning, replay reuse and an excessive PPO learning rate do under disclosed CPU budgets?
evaluation: Frozen tanh(mean)*physical_scale. Same five initial-state seeds at each evaluation. Continuing fixed target task, not generalization to other targets. Report return, mean/final distance, fraction of steps under .04m, final-32-step mean, wall time, interaction and optimizer counts.
analysis: Retain every seed and failed run. Median/IQR/range and paired per-seed differences at equal interaction budgets; descriptive only, no p-values or efficacy claim. PPO vs SAC are not equal-compute comparisons. Poor outcomes are valid. No selecting best seed for headline.
mechanisms: At five independent seeds, controlled ReLU neuron inactivation (zero incoming weights, bias -100) versus restoration at identical stored batch/noise; compare activations and actual actor gradients. This is induced inactivity, not evidence that ordinary training necessarily produces dormant neurons.
stop: Per-run hard budget 3600 seconds; record timeout/failed status and partial data. No silent retries or extensions. Pilot uses seed999 outside study and 512 interactions solely for timing, excluded from results.
